en: The *Dhāraṇī Scripture on the Collection of the Samādhi of Amitābha for Rebirth in the Nine Grades*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Special Advancement and Acting Chief of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra by imperial decree.
At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata was in the Great Samādhi-gate Mahāvihāra.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eighty-nine thousand bhikṣus,
all of whom were great arhats,
fully endowed with wisdom, and had accomplished all that was to be done.
Their names were: the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Supernatural Power and Eloquence; the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Supernatural Powers; and the Bodhisattva Pure Light Stainless Dhāraṇī.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Power Universally Heard, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Adornment Power,
the Bodhisattva Immeasurable Light, the Bodhisattva Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Good Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance King,
and such great bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas.
He went to where the Buddha was and said to him, "World-Honored One,
the Land of Immeasurable Life exists within the samādhi of the nine grades of pure consciousness;
it is the realm of all Buddhas and the abode of the Tathāgatas."
The Buddhas of the three periods of time attain perfect enlightenment from this;
they become fully endowed with the three types of supernormal knowledge and increase their merit and wisdom.
As for its nine grades of realms:
The highest grade of highest birth is the Stage of True Color;
the highest grade of middle birth is the Stainless Stage;
the highest grade of lowest birth is the Stage Free from Defilement.
Those of middle-grade superior birth attain the Ground of Excellent Awakening;
those of middle-grade middling birth attain the Ground of the Power of Clarity; those of middle-grade inferior birth attain the Ground of Outflowlessness.
Those of lower-grade superior birth attain the Ground of True Awakening.
The middle grade of the lower level is the Stage of Worthy Awakening;
the lower grade of the lower level is the Stage of the Gate of Joy.
These are called the nine grades of pure consciousness within the realm of True Suchness.
These are the precious images of the Great Round Mirror Wisdom within the twelve great maṇḍalas of the inner seat.
Their names are: the Buddha Infinite Light of All Threefold Knowledge (*traividyā*), and the Buddha Boundless Light of Universal Enlightenment in the Threefold Knowledge (*trividyā*).
The Buddha Jñānamārgatrayavidyānirargataprabha;
the Buddha Ṣaḍdharmatattvajñānatrayavidyāpratipakṣaprabha;
the Buddha Rūpasubhatrayavidyājvālārājaprabha.
The Buddha One-Awakening-Three-Knowledges-Pure-Light;
the Buddha Universal-Gate-Three-Knowledges-Joyful-Light;
the Buddha Entering-Wisdom-Three-Knowledges-Wisdom-Light.
The Buddha Uninterrupted Light of Radiance and the Three Knowledges;
the Buddha Inconceivable Light of Penetrating the Three Knowledges;
and the Buddha Irreproachable Light of the Five Virtues and the Three Knowledges.
The Buddha, whose wisdom-power and threefold clarity surpass the light of the sun and moon,
is thus a Tathāgata endowed with true form.
He is the locus of the compassionate manifestations of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
If there are sentient beings who wish to be reborn in such nine grades of pure lands,
they should reverently observe the twelve perfect wonders and recite the names of these nine grades of pure lands three times during the day and night.
By praising the names of the twelve Buddhas of Radiance,
one will forever emerge from the burning house of the three realms and will certainly give birth to True Suchness.
Having departed from the outflows (āsrava), one enters eternally into the state free from outflows (anāsrava).
If a person wishes to enter the sphere of such samādhi,
they should be endowed with the wisdom of a Buddha, purify their mind, and cleanse their body.
Contemplate the Great Samaya Reality Mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amṛtatejigalaṃ hūṃ. Noble son, such is this mantra, a Brahmanical incantation.
This seat is the ultimate wisdom and principle of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time;
it is the root of the twelve emptinesses and vows.
If my disciples wish to bring benefit and happiness to the triple world and to enrich humans and devas, [they should rely upon this].
Those who copy, uphold, read, and recite this sutra will increase their merit and happiness;
their wisdom and eloquence will be enhanced, and their lifespan, physical vigor, and strength will grow.
Their karmic obstacles will be eliminated, and all manner of illnesses will be extinguished.
If even those who merely increase their compassionate love possess perfect physical excellence,
how much more so for those who with a sincere heart copy, read, and recite it?
They shall transcend the three periods of time, realize non-arising, and escape the burning house of the triple world.
The assembly that had attained rebirth in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss and the nine grades of the Pure Land,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.

The *Kushō-hon* (Copy by Kankō) of the *Jūhon Ōjō Amida Kyō* (Sutra on Rebirth in the Nine Grades), copied and proofread on the eighth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of the Kenju era (1193) at Tōnomine,
using the original manuscript from the residence of the Ajari of Jizuin at Kanzeon-ji. Transcribed in the eighth month of autumn in the first year of the Kōwa era (1801).
I requested that the original manuscript of the *Jishan Jishun Sōjō Go-hon* be transcribed,
and then compared it against the printed edition.
Master Yu’s *Amida Daishin Shō* states:
This Great Heart Mantra is extracted from the *Amitāyus-vidhi* and the *Sūtra on Rebirth in the Nine Grades*.
It further states:
The *Kai-shaku Daishinju Shōnō* states that this is the same as what is taught in the *Kyūhon Ōjō Kyō*.
The *Jūshinron Guso* states:
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* (Nine Grades of Rebirth) states:
"This is the fundamental great mantra and dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Amitābha.
For one who recites it even once," [the merit is immeasurable].
"Then the ten evil deeds and the five crimes of immediate retribution within one's body—
all karmic obstructions— will be entirely extinguished," and so forth.
However, this original [text] contains only a short mantra.
There is no great incantation to be spoken;
one certainly knows that liberation is found in the great incantation-text.
Within this text, nothing is concealed or left unexpressed.
Readers should know that this awaits the complete edition.
Written by Kaidō at Chōdō, Hōzan Chōkoku.
Completed with one proofreading and additions by Cishun.
